TASK-001.gold_answer: A qualifying SBIR awardee must generally be a U.S.-based for-profit small business, satisfy applicable U.S. ownership and control requirements, and have no more than 500 employees including affiliates.

TASK-002.gold_answer: No. A nonprofit organization cannot directly receive an SBIR or STTR award.

TASK-003.gold_answer: At least 40% must be performed by the small business and at least 30% by the partnering research institution.

TASK-004.gold_answer: No. Under the normal SBIR Phase I performance-of-work rule, at least two-thirds of the research or analytical effort must be performed by the awardee.

TASK-006.gold_answer: No. Phase I proposers must first receive an official invitation following submission of a Project Pitch.

TASK-007.gold_answer: No. NSF Phase II proposals are limited to eligible NSF Phase I SBIR/STTR awardees.

TASK-008.gold_answer: Normally no. NSF considers employment elsewhere greater than 19.6 hours per week to conflict with its primary-employment requirement.
